name: Place Masséna
description: The main square of Nice, paved in a black-and-white checkerboard and framed by red-ochre arcaded buildings.

name: Jardin de la Pinède
description: A pine grove by the sea in Juan-les-Pins, near Antibes, where the Jazz à Juan festival has been held since 1960.

name: Cours Saleya
description: A long square in the old town that holds a daily flower and produce market.

name: Villa Nellcôte
description: A seaside villa in Villefranche-sur-Mer, east of Nice, where the Rolling Stones recorded much of an album in 1971.

name: Musée Picasso, Antibes
description: A museum in the Grimaldi castle in Antibes, where Pablo Picasso worked in 1946. It holds the works he made there.

name: Villa Isola Bella
description: A villa in Menton, near the Italian border, where the New Zealand writer Katherine Mansfield lived in 1920 and 1921.

name: Casino de Monte-Carlo
description: The 19th-century casino in Monaco, whose building also holds the Monte-Carlo Opera.

name: Former Palais Croisette
description: The site of the first festival hall in Cannes, which hosted the Cannes Film Festival from 1949 to 1982.

name: Musée Matisse
description: A museum in a 17th-century villa in Cimiez, the hill neighborhood where the painter Henri Matisse lived and is buried.

name: Hôtel Belles Rives
description: A seaside hotel in Juan-les-Pins, once a villa where the American writer F. Scott Fitzgerald lived in 1926.

name: Studios de la Victorine
description: Film studios in western Nice, founded in 1919, where many French and foreign films have been shot.

name: Palais de la Méditerranée
description: An Art Deco casino on the seafront, opened in 1929. Only the facade of the original building survives, in front of a hotel.

name: Chapelle du Rosaire
description: A small chapel in Vence designed by the painter Henri Matisse and completed in 1951, with his stained glass and wall drawings.
